You are building the viewer for this repository's hackathon entry, on branch `viewer` in a git worktree, in parallel with the main build on `main`. Jacob Schoenberg approved the spec (docs/spec.md) on 2026-11-05, and a setup session launched you headless. First read CLAUDE.md, every file in .claude/rules/, docs/spec.md ("Viewer and video") and the "## Log format" section of docs/BUILD_NOTES.md. That last file is in the main checkout at ../digital-life/docs/BUILD_NOTES.md; re-read it from there, because it may update while you work.

WORKING STYLE (required; an earlier build session died because one reply was too large and timed out)
- Write one file per tool call, each under about 200 lines, and never several files in one reply. Split big files.
- Keep replies short: one or two tool calls per step. Read files in ranges, grep for functions, and never re-read a file.
- Commit after each piece that works, so progress survives a crash.

GOAL: a viewer that replays any run directory: the map, bees and hornets moving, seasons, sounds, stings, hatchings, and a clicked bee's recent decisions and memories. The same viewer has to produce the frames for the demo video later, so it must render deterministically from the logs alone.

BUILD
1. Everything lives under viewer/, so this branch merges cleanly. Touch nothing outside viewer/ apart from the agent_traces files your hooks write.
2. viewer/bundle.py RUN_DIR [-o out.html] writes ONE self-contained HTML file with the run's data inlined (compressed if large). It must open from file:// on any machine with no server, so judges can open it and the headless capture works.
3. The page: canvas rendering of the layout and the per-tick state, a play/pause button, a timeline slider, a speed control, and a season indicator done as a colour tint plus small text.
   - Bees are warm yellow, with a thin ring showing life left. Carrying bees get a dot.
   - Hornets are orange-brown, distinct from the bees at small sizes.
   - Bloom cells, and the hive with its entrances.
   - Sound ripples of radius 10: sound-1 teal, sound-2 magenta.
   - Sting flash, hatch sparkle, death fade.
   - A side panel for the selected bee: its id, life, and its recent decisions (intent, sound, remember, say) from the events log.
   - Interaction: exact-point tap or click to select (hit-test the real drawn position), pinch and wheel zoom, drag to pan.
   - The look is clean and readable at 1280x720 video size. No decorative mono labels, kickers or counters. Use plain words and a light, warm paper background.
4. A capture mode, URL hash #capture&from=T0&to=T1&step=S, that steps through ticks deterministically, so a script can screenshot each frame.
5. viewer/capture.py RUN_HTML OUT.mp4 --from --to --step --fps renders frames headlessly with the Playwright headless shell ([REDACTED:path-outside-repo], run with --no-sandbox and a --user-data-dir on /dev/shm) and encodes them with ffmpeg. Frames go on /dev/shm and are deleted after encoding. Snap Chromium cannot read /tmp, so don't use it.
6. Develop against a small synthetic fixture you generate in the documented log format (viewer/fixtures/, a few hundred KB at most). When real runs exist in the main checkout (../digital-life/experiments/results/), test against them too. A smoke test (viewer/test_viewer.py, plain pytest) bundles the fixture and checks the HTML loads and renders a frame headlessly.
7. A one-line section at the top of viewer/README.md giving the bundle and capture commands.

RULES
- Commit small and often on branch `viewer`. Push with `.local/push.sh -q origin viewer`. Never push to main and never merge; the orchestrator merges. Never rewrite history.
- Use ../digital-life/.venv/bin/python for Python. Don't install heavy packages; Playwright's Python package is not needed, since the headless shell binary is called directly through its CLI or the DevTools protocol.
- The shared VM's disk is tight. Put frames and scratch on /dev/shm and delete them when done.
- No model calls. No GitHub. Never print secrets.
- Stop when 1 to 7 work. End with a short report and the exact commands.

# Spec: a bee colony against evolving hornets (working title)

Approved by Jacob Schoenberg on 2026-11-05. Numbers marked (tune) are starting values, calibrated with scripted bees before any AI run. Every calibration is recorded in EXPERIMENTS.md under "Setup calibration".

**Primary property: adaptation, at three speeds,** under seasonal change:
- individual memory, within one bee's life;
- colony knowledge passed on inside the hive, across bee generations;
- genetic evolution, in the hornets.

Supporting properties: persistence (knowledge outliving every bee that gained it), interaction (two sounds, talk inside the hive) and emergence (whether the sounds come to mean something).

## World

- **Grid:** 80 x 48 cells, 4-neighbour moves. Walls are generated from the seed as a braided maze: corridors, rooms and loops, with several routes between any two areas. The layout stays fixed for the whole run.
- **Hive:** a room at the left edge, about 6 x 8 inside, with 3 entrances. Hornets cannot enter hive cells.
- **Bloom sites:**
  - Three sites in the right half, one each for spring, summer and autumn. Each is a 3 x 3 patch, placed from the seed with a minimum path distance from the hive (tune).
  - The sites repeat every year, so year 2's spring bloom is where year 1's was.
- **Time:**
  - Ticks. Four seasons of 250 ticks each (spring, summer, autumn, winter), and 2 years, so 2,000 ticks per run. Both lengths are configurable; the demo uses a smaller map and one short year.
  - Seasons are never named to the bees. Bees only experience their effects.
- **Winter:**
  - There is no bloom.
  - A bee outside the hive loses 2 life per tick; inside, 0.5 per tick (fractions accumulate).
  - Hornets are dormant and off the map.

## Bees

- **Colony size:** at most 12 alive. The colony starts with 6.
- **Queen floor:** whenever fewer than 2 bees are alive, the queen (not an agent) hatches a blank bee in the hive. Logged as `queen_hatch`.
- **Life:** base L = 250 (tune). One unit is lost per tick, at winter rates in winter. A bee dies at 0.
- **Delivery:**
  - Reaching any bloom cell sets `carrying`.
  - Entering the hive while carrying doubles the bee's life, capped at 3 x L, and clears `carrying`.
  - If fewer than 12 bees are alive, a new bee hatches with life L and no memories.
- **Sting:**
  - A hornet adjacent to a bee (Manhattan distance 1) can sting it.
  - A sting removes half the bee's current life (rounded down) and stuns the bee for 2 ticks.
  - The same hornet cannot sting the same bee again for 10 ticks, so a bee can't be stung into a lock.
  - The hornet's reward is the life it removed.
- **Healing:** once per life, a stung bee that enters the hive recovers half of the life it lost to stings. This happens automatically.
- **Senses:**
  - Vision radius 4 (square): walls, open cells, other bees, hornets.
  - Bloom cells are visible from 6.
  - Sounds are heard within 10 (Euclidean), reported as which sound, an 8-way direction and a distance band.
  - Each bee knows its own position, its home's position, its life left and whether it is carrying.
- **Sounds:**
  - Two neutral sounds, `sound-1` and `sound-2`. Under the `labels_good_bad` condition they are called "good noise" and "bad noise".
  - A bee makes a sound as part of a decision, and it costs 1 extra life.

## Bee mind (AI)

- **Model:** `claude-haiku-5-5`, effort low, thinking disabled, structured output. All calls go through `digital_life.llm.complete` with `tag = f"{seed}:{tick}:{bee_id}:{condition}"`.
- **When a bee decides:** every 5 ticks, and immediately on an event:
  - it is stung;
  - it newly sees a hornet;
  - it sees bloom;
  - it hears a sound;
  - it arrives at its target;
  - it enters the hive;
  - its life crosses 50% or 25%.
- **Decision (schema):**
  - `intent`: one of `explore` (with an 8-way direction), `go_to` (with x, y), `go_home`, `flee` or `wait`;
  - `sound`: `none`, `sound-1` or `sound-2`;
  - `remember`: a short belief, or empty;
  - `say`: up to 30 words, used only inside the hive, and heard by every bee in the hive that tick.
- **Motor layer (no AI):** executes the intent using only that bee's own known map, meaning cells it has seen.
  - Movement uses A* over known cells. Unknown cells count as passable, and the route is replanned when a wall turns up.
  - `explore` heads for the nearest unexplored frontier in the chosen direction.
  - `flee` moves to maximise distance from the hornets the bee can see.
- **Neutral prompt:**
  - The system prompt lives in one file, `prompts/bee_system.txt`. It says only that:
    - your life is a number that falls each moment and ends at zero;
    - something worth finding exists in this place;
    - you are one of many identical members of your home;
    - here is what you can perceive and do.
  - It never mentions bees, hives, flowers, hornets, food, danger or seasons. The viewer draws bees and hornets; the model never hears those words.
- **Perception text:**
  - own position, home position, life left, carrying;
  - the local view as symbols;
  - moving things and bright cells in view;
  - sounds heard;
  - recalled memories;
  - things heard at home;
  - landmarks from the bee's known map: home, bright spots seen, where moving things were seen, and how much has been explored in each direction.
- **Memory (local, free):**
  - **Short-term:** the last 8 events.
  - **Episodes:** a log with rule-based importance (sting 5, delivery 5, bloom seen 4, hornet seen 3, sound heard 1).
  - **Beliefs:** up to 12 short texts written through `remember`; the oldest is evicted.
  - **Recall:** the top 6 by recency, importance and BM25 relevance to the current situation.
- **Hive talk:**
  - `say` inside the hive is heard by every bee in the hive that tick, and stored as "heard at home".
  - Newborns stay inside for their first 3 ticks.
  - There is no separate reflection call. Arriving home triggers a decision, and `say` is available then.

## Hornets (no AI)

- **Count:** 4 in spring, 6 in summer, 8 in autumn, 0 in winter (dormant).
- **Genome:** 10 points spread over 3 genes:
  - `smell`: the range at which it detects bees;
  - `hearing`: how strongly it is drawn to bee sounds, and from how far;
  - `ambush`: how much it waits at places where it stung before, or near bloom, instead of roaming.
- **Behaviour each tick:**
  - If a bee is within smell range, pick a target with probability proportional to the bee's life, and step toward it. Hornets path on the true map, since they are part of the environment.
  - Otherwise, if a sound is within hearing range, move toward it with a probability set by the gene.
  - Otherwise, ambush or wander as the genes set.
- **Fitness:** life removed per tick alive.
- **Evolution:**
  - Every 25 ticks outside winter, the least fit hornet is replaced by a copy of a hornet chosen in proportion to fitness. The copy is mutated: with probability 0.5, one point moves between genes.
  - At the end of winter, the spring hornets are bred from the fittest hornets of the previous autumn.
- **`frozen_hornets` condition:** genes stay at their initial random draw (same seed).

## Conditions

| Condition | What changes |
|---|---|
| `full` | Everything above, neutral sounds |
| `no_talk` | `say` disabled; nothing is heard at home |
| `no_memory` | No episodes, beliefs or recall; the bee decides from current perception only |
| `frozen_hornets` | No hornet evolution |
| `rule_bees` | Scripted bees: explore at random, go home at half life, never share. No AI |
| `random_bees` | Random intents. No AI |
| `labels_good_bad` | The sounds are called "good noise" and "bad noise" |
| `oracle_bees` | Calibration only, never reported as a result: scripted bees told where the bloom is |

## Logging

- **Per tick:** every bee's position, life, carrying, stunned and intent; every hornet's position, genes and target; sounds made.
- **Events:** sting, delivery, hatch, queen_hatch, death, heal, say, decision.
- **Per run:** the world layout (walls, hive, entrances, bloom sites), plus per-season metrics and a run summary.
- Writes go through `RunLog`. Per-tick state goes to a compact JSONL file that the viewer reads.

## Viewer and video

- **Viewer:** a static `viewer/` page (HTML, canvas, JS) that loads a run directory. It shows:
  - a top-down map with a seasonal tint;
  - bees in yellow, with a ring showing life left;
  - hornets in orange-brown;
  - the bloom;
  - sound ripples of radius 10 (sound-1 teal, sound-2 magenta);
  - sting flashes and hatch sparkles;
  - a timeline slider and play/pause;
  - a selected bee's recent memories and intents, when clicked.
- **Video:** frames captured headless from the viewer (Playwright chrome-headless-shell, files on /dev/shm), then encoded with ffmpeg. The video is made last, from a fresh clone.

## Demo

`make demo` runs a small map (about 40 x 24, one short year) with rule bees, which needs no key. It also replays one recorded AI run from `experiments/llm_cache/`.
======
# Build notes (handoff between build phases)

Written by the phase 1 build session (Claude Code, 2026-11-06). Phase 1 is the world with no AI: layout, seasons, evolving hornets, scripted bees, logging, tests and calibration. Later phases plug the AI mind in through the policy interface below.

## Log format

Format version 1. Every seed of every run writes one run directory:

```
experiments/results/<experiment>/<UTC stamp>[_<tag>]/seed-<n>/
    record.json        written by experiments/run.py: params, seed, provenance, final_metrics (the run summary)
    layout.json        the world, written once before tick 0
    state.jsonl.gz     gzip-compressed JSONL, one line per tick: positions and state of everything
    events.jsonl       one line per event
    metrics.jsonl      one line per season
```

Coordinates are `[x, y]` with x to the right and y downward, 0-based. Moves are 4-neighbour.

### layout.json

```json
{
  "format": 1,
  "width": 80, "height": 48,
  "rows": ["#####...", "#HHH...", "..."],
  "home": [3, 23],
  "entrances": [[7, 22], [4, 19], [4, 28]],
  "bloom": {"spring": [[x, y], ...9 cells], "summer": [...], "autumn": [...]},
  "bloom_distance": {"spring": 61, "summer": 74, "autumn": 58},
  "season_names": ["spring", "summer", "autumn", "winter"],
  "season_length": 250, "years": 2, "ticks": 2000,
  "base_life": 250, "life_cap": 750, "max_bees": 12,
  "vision": 4, "bloom_vision": 6, "hearing": 10,
  "condition": "rule_bees", "seed": 0,
  "bee_fields": ["id", "x", "y", "life", "carrying", "stunned", "intent"],
  "hornet_fields": ["id", "x", "y", "smell", "hearing", "ambush", "target", "mode"],
  "sound_fields": ["bee", "x", "y", "sound"]
}
```

- `rows`: `height` strings of `width` characters. `#` wall, `.` open, `H` hive interior, `E` hive entrance. Entrances count as hive cells: hornets never stand on `H` or `E`.
- `home`: the hive's centre cell, the position every bee is told is home.
- `bloom`: the 3 x 3 patch for each season. Winter has none. The same cells bloom every year.
- `bloom_distance`: shortest path in steps from `home` to the nearest cell of each patch.

### state.jsonl.gz

One JSON object per tick, written after the tick has resolved:

```json
{"t": 0, "s": 0, "y": 0,
 "b": [[0, 3, 23, 249.0, 0, 0, "explore:NE"], ...],
 "h": [[0, 52, 11, 4, 3, 3, -1, "wander"], ...],
 "snd": [[2, 40, 18, "sound-1"]]}
```

- `t` tick (0-based), `s` season index (0 spring, 1 summer, 2 autumn, 3 winter), `y` year (0-based).
- `b`, one array per living bee, in `bee_fields` order: id, x, y, life (1 decimal), carrying (0 or 1), stunned (ticks of stun left, 0 if not stunned), intent.
  - intent is one of `explore:<dir>` (dir is N, NE, E, SE, S, SW, W or NW), `go_to:<x>,<y>`, `go_home`, `flee`, `wait`, or `""` before the bee's first decision.
- `h`, one array per hornet on the map, in `hornet_fields` order: id, x, y, the three genes, target (bee id, or -1), mode (`chase`, `sound`, `ambush` or `wander`). Empty in winter.
- `snd`, sounds made this tick: bee id, x, y, `sound-1` or `sound-2`. Other bees and hornets hear them on the next tick.

Read it in a browser with `new Response(blob.stream().pipeThrough(new DecompressionStream("gzip"))).text()`, then split on newlines.

### events.jsonl

One object per line. Every event has `kind` and `t`.

| kind | fields |
|---|---|
| `season` | season (name), year |
| `hatch` | bee, x, y, life, cause (`start` for the founding bees, `delivery` otherwise) |
| `queen_hatch` | bee, x, y, life |
| `decision` | bee, trigger, intent, direction, target, sound, remember, say |
| `say` | bee, text, heard_by (list of bee ids) |
| `bloom` | bee, x, y (the bee picked up from bloom and is now carrying) |
| `delivery` | bee, life_before, life_after |
| `heal` | bee, amount, life_after |
| `sting` | hornet, bee, x, y, amount, life_after |
| `death` | bee, x, y, age, cause (`life`: life reached 0) |
| `trip` | bee, start, ticks, delivered, reached_bloom (ticks from leaving to reaching bloom, or null), stings, outcome (`home` or `died`) |
| `hornet_spawn` | hornet, x, y, genes ([smell, hearing, ambush]), parent (hornet id or null) |
| `hornet_replaced` | removed, removed_fitness, parent, child, genes |
| `hornet_dormant` | hornets (list of [id, smell, hearing, ambush, fitness]) |
| `end` | bees_alive |

`decision.trigger` is one of `timer`, `stung`, `hornet`, `bloom`, `sound`, `arrived`, `home`, `life50`, `life25`, `hatched`. Decision `target` is `[x, y]` or null; `direction` is a direction string or null.

### metrics.jsonl

One row per season, written at the season's last tick (`step`):

| field | meaning |
|---|---|
| `step`, `year`, `season` | last tick of the season, year (0-based), season name |
| `trips` | trips that started this season (a trip starts when a bee steps out of the hive) |
| `deliveries` | deliveries this season |
| `delivery_rate` | deliveries / trips, null if no trips |
| `stings`, `stings_per_trip` | stings this season, and stings / trips |
| `median_to_bloom` | median ticks from leaving the hive to reaching bloom, over trips that reached it; null if none |
| `first_delivery` | ticks after the season's start of its first delivery; null if none |
| `bees_end`, `bees_mean` | colony size at the season's end, and mean over its ticks |
| `hatches`, `queen_hatches`, `deaths` | counts this season |
| `sounds_1`, `sounds_2` | sounds made this season |
| `hornets`, `smell`, `hearing`, `ambush` | hornets on the map at the season's end, and their mean genes (null in winter) |
| `hornet_damage` | life removed by stings this season |

"""Write a small synthetic run directory in the documented log format (format 1).

This is a viewer test fixture, not a result: scripted movers on a 40 x 24 map
that exercise every event kind the viewer draws. Deterministic for a given seed.

    python viewer/fixtures/make_fixture.py [OUT_DIR] [--seed N]
"""
import argparse
import gzip
import json
import random
from collections import deque
from pathlib import Path

W, H, SEASON, YEARS, BASE_LIFE, MAX_BEES = 40, 24, 40, 1, 120, 12
SEASONS = ["spring", "summer", "autumn", "winter"]
HORNETS_PER_SEASON = [3, 4, 5, 0]
DIRS = {"N": (0, -1), "NE": (1, -1), "E": (1, 0), "SE": (1, 1),
        "S": (0, 1), "SW": (-1, 1), "W": (-1, 0), "NW": (-1, -1)}
BELIEFS = ["bright cells lie far to the east", "the moving things wait near bright cells",
           "the upper corridor is quieter", "sound two came before the sting",
           "home is west, follow the long corridor back", "bright spot moved since last time"]
SAYS = ["bright cells east past the second room", "avoid the lower corridor, I was hit there",
        "the second sound meant danger to me", "nothing found north"]


def make_map(rng):
    g = [["#"] * W for _ in range(H)]
    stack, seen = [(9, 1)], {(9, 1)}
    g[1][9] = "."
    while stack:  # carve a maze on odd cells, x >= 9 (the hive sits to the left)
        x, y = stack[-1]
        nxt = [(x + dx, y + dy, dx, dy) for dx, dy in ((2, 0), (-2, 0), (0, 2), (0, -2))
               if 9 <= x + dx < W - 1 and 1 <= y + dy < H - 1 and (x + dx, y + dy) not in seen]
        if not nxt:
            stack.pop()
            continue
        nx, ny, dx, dy = rng.choice(nxt)
        g[y + dy // 2][x + dx // 2] = g[ny][nx] = "."
        seen.add((nx, ny))
        stack.append((nx, ny))
    for y in range(1, H - 1):  # braid: knock out walls to make loops and rooms
        for x in range(9, W - 1):
            if g[y][x] == "#" and rng.random() < 0.3:
                g[y][x] = "."
    for y in range(8, 16):
        for x in range(1, 8):
            g[y][x] = "H"
    entrances = [(8, 9), (8, 12), (8, 15)]
    for x, y in entrances:
        g[y][x] = "E"
        g[y][9] = "."
    bloom = {}
    for name, (cx, cy) in zip(SEASONS[:3], [(rng.randint(22, 27), rng.randint(3, 6)),
                                            (rng.randint(32, 36), rng.randint(10, 13)),
                                            (rng.randint(24, 30), rng.randint(17, 20))]):
        bloom[name] = [(cx + i, cy + j) for j in (-1, 0, 1) for i in (-1, 0, 1)]
        for x, y in bloom[name]:
            g[y][x] = "."
    return g, entrances, bloom


def bfs(g, start, passable):
    dist, prev, q = {start: 0}, {start: None}, deque([start])
    while q:
        x, y = q.popleft()
        for dx, dy in ((1, 0), (-1, 0), (0, 1), (0, -1)):
            n = (x + dx, y + dy)
            if 0 <= n[0] < W and 0 <= n[1] < H and n not in dist and passable(g[n[1]][n[0]]):
                dist[n], prev[n] = dist[(x, y)] + 1, (x, y)
                q.append(n)
    return dist, prev


def step_toward(g, a, goals, passable):
    dist, prev = bfs(g, a, passable)
    reach = [c for c in goals if c in dist]
    if not reach:
        return a
    c = min(reach, key=dist.get)
    while prev[c] is not None and prev[c] != a:
        c = prev[c]
    return c


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("out", nargs="?", default=str(Path(__file__).parent / "synthetic-run"))
    ap.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=7)
    args = ap.parse_args()
    rng = random.Random(args.seed)
    g, entrances, bloom = make_map(rng)
    home = (4, 12)
    hive = [(x, y) for y in range(H) for x in range(W) if g[y][x] in "HE"]
    open_out = [(x, y) for y in range(H) for x in range(W) if g[y][x] == "."]
    bee_ok, hornet_ok = (lambda c: c != "#"), (lambda c: c == ".")
    dist_home, _ = bfs(g, home, bee_ok)

    layout = {

        "bloom_distance": {k: min(dist_home[c] for c in v) for k, v in bloom.items()},
        "season_names": SEASONS, "season_length": SEASON, "years": YEARS, "ticks": ticks,
        "base_life": BASE_LIFE, "life_cap": 3 * BASE_LIFE, "max_bees": MAX_BEES,
        "vision": 4, "bloom_vision": 6, "hearing": 10, "condition": "synthetic", "seed": args.seed,
        "bee_fields": ["id", "x", "y", "life", "carrying", "stunned", "intent"],
        "hornet_fields": ["id", "x", "y", "smell", "hearing", "ambush", "target", "mode"],

    events, states, metrics = [], [], []
    ev = lambda kind, t, **kw: events.append({"kind": kind, "t": t, **kw})
    bees, hornets, next_bee, next_hornet = {}, {}, 0, 0
    season_count = {}

    def hatch(t, kind, cause=None):
        nonlocal next_bee
        x, y = rng.choice(hive)
        bees[next_bee] = {"x": x, "y": y, "life": float(BASE_LIFE), "carry": 0, "stun": 0,
                          "intent": "", "born": t, "goal": None, "cool": {}, "rest": 3}
        kw = {"cause": cause} if cause else {}
        ev(kind, t, bee=next_bee, x=x, y=y, life=float(BASE_LIFE), **kw)
        next_bee += 1

    for _ in range(4):
        hatch(0, "hatch", "start")
    for t in range(ticks):
        s, yr = (t // SEASON) % 4, t // (SEASON * 4)
        if t % SEASON == 0:
            ev("season", t, season=SEASONS[s], year=yr)
            season_count = {"stings": 0, "deliveries": 0, "hatches": 0, "deaths": 0, "s1": 0, "s2": 0}
            if s == 3:
                ev("hornet_dormant", t, hornets=[[i, *h["genes"], 0.0] for i, h in hornets.items()])
                hornets.clear()
        while s < 3 and len(hornets) < HORNETS_PER_SEASON[s]:
            x, y = rng.choice([c for c in open_out if c[0] > 20])
            genes = [rng.randint(1, 6)]
            genes += [rng.randint(0, 10 - genes[0])]
            genes.append(10 - genes[0] - genes[1])
            hornets[next_hornet] = {"x": x, "y": y, "genes": genes, "target": -1, "mode": "wander"}

                    mem = rng.choice(BELIEFS) if rng.random() < 0.4 else ""
                    snd = "none"

                       target=None if goal == [home] else list(goal[4]), sound=snd, remember=mem,
                       say=rng.choice(SAYS) if in_hive and rng.random() < 0.5 else "")
                    if in_hive and events[-1]["say"]:

                        ev("say", t, bee=i, text=events[-1]["say"], heard_by=heard)

                b["x"], b["y"] = step_toward(g, pos, goal, bee_ok)
            near = any(abs(h["x"] - b["x"]) + abs(h["y"] - b["y"]) <= 4 for h in hornets.values())
            if (near and rng.random() < 0.15) or (b["carry"] and rng.random() < 0.03):
                snd = "sound-2" if near else "sound-1"
                sounds.append([i, b["x"], b["y"], snd])
                season_count["s1" if snd == "sound-1" else "s2"] += 1
                b["life"] -= 1
            if not b["carry"] and s < 3 and (b["x"], b["y"]) in bloom[SEASONS[s]]:
                b["carry"] = 1
                ev("bloom", t, bee=i, x=b["x"], y=b["y"])
            if b["carry"] and g[b["y"]][b["x"]] in "HE":
                before = b["life"]
                b["life"], b["carry"], b["rest"] = min(before * 2, 3 * BASE_LIFE), 0, 2
                ev("delivery", t, bee=i, life_before=before, life_after=b["life"])
                season_count["deliveries"] += 1
                if len(bees) < MAX_BEES:
                    hatch(t, "hatch", "delivery")
                    season_count["hatches"] += 1
            if b["life"] <= 0:
                ev("death", t, bee=i, x=b["x"], y=b["y"], age=t - b["born"], cause="life")

        for k, h in hornets.items():
            prey = [(abs(b["x"] - h["x"]) + abs(b["y"] - h["y"]), i) for i, b in bees.items()
                    if g[b["y"]][b["x"]] == "."]
            prey = [p for p in prey if p[0] <= h["genes"][0] + 2]
            if prey:
                d, i = min(prey)
                b = bees[i]
                h["target"], h["mode"] = i, "chase"
                if d == 1 and b["life"] > 2 and t - b["cool"].get(k, -99) >= 10:
                    amt = int(b["life"] // 2)
                    b["life"] -= amt
                    b["stun"], b["cool"][k] = 2, t
                    ev("sting", t, hornet=k, bee=i, x=b["x"], y=b["y"], amount=amt, life_after=b["life"])
                    season_count["stings"] += 1
                elif d > 1:
                    h["x"], h["y"] = step_toward(g, (h["x"], h["y"]), [(b["x"], b["y"])], hornet_ok)
            else:
                h["target"], h["mode"] = -1, "wander"
                opts = [(h["x"] + dx, h["y"] + dy) for dx, dy in ((1, 0), (-1, 0), (0, 1), (0, -1))
                        if g[h["y"] + dy][h["x"] + dx] == "."]
                h["x"], h["y"] = rng.choice(opts) if opts else (h["x"], h["y"])
        if len(bees) < 2:
            hatch(t, "queen_hatch")
        states.append({"t": t, "s": s, "y": yr,
                       "b": [[i, b["x"], b["y"], round(b["life"], 1), b["carry"], b["stun"], b["intent"]]
                             for i, b in bees.items()],
                       "h": [[k, h["x"], h["y"], *h["genes"], h["target"], h["mode"]] for k, h in hornets.items()],
                       "snd": sounds})
        if t % SEASON == SEASON - 1:
            metrics.append({"step": t, "year": yr, "season": SEASONS[s], "bees_end": len(bees),
                            "deliveries": season_count["deliveries"], "stings": season_count["stings"],
                            "hatches": season_count["hatches"], "deaths": season_count["deaths"],
                            "sounds_1": season_count["s1"], "sounds_2": season_count["s2"],
                            "hornets": len(hornets)})
    ev("end", ticks - 1, bees_alive=len(bees))
    with gzip.GzipFile(out / "state.jsonl.gz", "wb", mtime=0) as f:
        f.write("".join(json.dumps(s, separators=(",", ":")) + "\n" for s in states).encode())
    (out / "events.jsonl").write_text("".join(json.dumps(e) + "\n" for e in events))
    (out / "metrics.jsonl").write_text("".join(json.dumps(m) + "\n" for m in metrics))
    (out / "record.json").write_text(json.dumps({"synthetic": True, "note": "viewer test fixture, not a result",
                                                 "seed": args.seed}, indent=1))

"""Bundle one run directory into a single self-contained HTML page that replays it.

    python viewer/bundle.py RUN_DIR [-o out.html]

The page needs no server and no network: the run's logs are inlined (state and events
gzip-compressed, base64-encoded) and decompressed in the browser. Open it from file://.
"""
import argparse
import base64
import gzip
import json
import re
from pathlib import Path

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
SRC = HERE / "src"
JS_FILES = ["data.js", "draw_map.js", "draw_live.js", "panel.js", "input.js", "app.js"]


def _gz_b64(raw: bytes) -> str:
    return base64.b64encode(gzip.compress(raw, compresslevel=9, mtime=0)).decode("ascii")


def _read_maybe_gz(run_dir: Path, name: str) -> bytes | None:
    """Raw bytes of NAME or NAME.gz, decompressed. None if neither exists."""
    if (run_dir / name).exists():
        return (run_dir / name).read_bytes()
    if (run_dir / (name + ".gz")).exists():
        return gzip.decompress((run_dir / (name + ".gz")).read_bytes())
    return None


def run_name(run_dir: Path) -> str:
    """A readable name: up to the last three path parts (experiment/stamp/seed-n)."""
    parts = run_dir.resolve().parts
    return "/".join(parts[-3:])


def load_run(run_dir: Path) -> dict:
    run_dir = Path(run_dir)
    layout = json.loads((run_dir / "layout.json").read_text())
    if layout.get("format", 1) != 1:
        raise SystemExit(f"{run_dir}: layout format {layout.get('format')} is not supported (expected 1)")
    state = _read_maybe_gz(run_dir, "state.jsonl")
    if state is None:
        raise SystemExit(f"{run_dir}: no state.jsonl.gz")
    events = _read_maybe_gz(run_dir, "events.jsonl") or b""
    metrics_raw = _read_maybe_gz(run_dir, "metrics.jsonl") or b""
    metrics = [json.loads(line) for line in metrics_raw.decode().splitlines() if line.strip()]
    return {
        "name": run_name(run_dir),
        "layout": layout,
        "state": _gz_b64(state),
        "events": _gz_b64(events),
        "metrics": metrics,
    }


def _inline_json(obj) -> str:
    # "</" would end the <script> element early; "<\/" is the same string to JSON and JS.
    return json.dumps(obj, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False).replace("</", "<\\/")


def build_html(run_dir: Path) -> str:
    data = load_run(run_dir)
    template = (SRC / "index.html").read_text()
    css = (SRC / "style.css").read_text()
    js = "\n".join(f"// ---- {name}\n" + (SRC / name).read_text() for name in JS_FILES)
    title = re.sub(r"[<>&\"]", "", f"Bee colony, {data['layout'].get('condition', '')} seed {data['layout'].get('seed', '')}")
    html = template.replace("/*__CSS__*/", css).replace("/*__JS__*/", js.replace("</script", "<\\/script"))
    html = html.replace("__TITLE__", title)
    head, tail = html.split("__DATA__", 1)
    return head + _inline_json(data) + tail


def main(argv=None):
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    ap.add_argument("run_dir", type=Path, help="a run directory (holds layout.json and state.jsonl.gz)")
    ap.add_argument("-o", "--out", type=Path, help="output HTML (default viewer/out/<run>.html)")
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)
    out = args.out or HERE / "out" / (re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9._-]+", "_", run_name(args.run_dir)) + ".html")
    out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    out.write_text(build_html(args.run_dir), encoding="utf-8")
    print(f"{out} ({out.stat().st_size / 1024:.0f} KB)")
    return out


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Render a bundled viewer page to video (or one still), headless and deterministic.

    python viewer/capture.py RUN_HTML OUT.mp4 --from 0 --to 400 --step 0.5 --fps 30
    python viewer/capture.py RUN_HTML still.png --from 120 [--bee 3]

Each frame is the page in capture mode (#capture&from=..&to=..&step=..) rendering tick
from + i * step from the inlined logs alone, then screenshotted. Frames go to a scratch
directory on /dev/shm and are deleted after ffmpeg encodes them.
"""
import argparse
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))
from cdp import Browser, CDPError, scratch_dir  # noqa: E402


def capture_hash(t0, t1=None, step=1.0, bee=None, view=None):
    h = f"#capture&from={t0:g}&step={step:g}"
    if t1 is not None:
        h += f"&to={t1:g}"
    if bee is not None:
        h += f"&bee={bee}"
    if view:
        h += f"&view={view}"
    return h


def open_page(browser, html: Path, hash_: str, timeout=120):
    """Load the page in capture mode and return its frame count."""
    browser.goto(html.resolve().as_uri() + hash_)
    browser.wait_for("window.__viewerReady === true || !!window.__viewerError", timeout=timeout)
    err = browser.eval("window.__viewerError || null")
    if err:
        raise CDPError("the viewer failed to load: " + err)
    return browser.eval("window.__capture.count")


def render_frames(browser, frames_dir: Path, count: int, quiet=False):
    start = time.monotonic()
    for i in range(count):
        browser.eval(f"window.__capture.frame({i})")
        (frames_dir / f"f{i:06d}.png").write_bytes(browser.screenshot())
        if not quiet and (i + 1) % 100 == 0:
            rate = (i + 1) / (time.monotonic() - start)
            print(f"  frame {i + 1} of {count} ({rate:.1f} per second)", file=sys.stderr)


def encode(frames_dir: Path, out: Path, fps: float):
    cmd = ["ffmpeg", "-y", "-loglevel", "error", "-framerate", f"{fps:g}", "-i", str(frames_dir / "f%06d.png"),
           "-c:v", "libx264", "-preset", "medium", "-crf", "18", "-pix_fmt", "yuv420p",
           "-movflags", "+faststart", str(out)]
    subprocess.run(cmd, check=True)


def main(argv=None):
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Render a bundled viewer page to MP4 or PNG, headless.")
    ap.add_argument("html", type=Path, help="a page written by viewer/bundle.py")
    ap.add_argument("out", type=Path, help="output .mp4, or .png for a single still at --from")
    ap.add_argument("--from", dest="t0", type=float, default=0.0, help="first tick (default 0)")
    ap.add_argument("--to", dest="t1", type=float, default=None, help="last tick (default: the run's last)")
    ap.add_argument("--step", type=float, default=0.5, help="ticks per frame (default 0.5)")
    ap.add_argument("--fps", type=float, default=30.0, help="frames per second of video (default 30)")
    ap.add_argument("--bee", type=int, default=None, help="select this bee, so the panel follows it")
    ap.add_argument("--view", default=None, help="frame a region of cells: x0,y0,x1,y1")
    ap.add_argument("--size", default="1280x720", help="viewport WIDTHxHEIGHT (default 1280x720)")
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)
    if args.step <= 0:
        ap.error("--step must be positive")
    if not args.html.exists():
        ap.error(f"{args.html} does not exist")
    width, height = (int(v) for v in args.size.lower().split("x"))
    still = args.out.suffix.lower() == ".png"
    hash_ = capture_hash(args.t0, args.t0 if still else args.t1, args.step, args.bee, args.view)
    args.out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    with Browser(width, height) as browser:
        count = open_page(browser, args.html, hash_)
        if still:
            browser.eval("window.__capture.frame(0)")
            args.out.write_bytes(browser.screenshot())
            print(args.out)
            return args.out
        if shutil.which("ffmpeg") is None:
            raise SystemExit("ffmpeg is not on PATH")
        print(f"{count} frames, {count / args.fps:.1f} s of video", file=sys.stderr)
        frames_dir = Path(scratch_dir("viewer-frames-"))
        try:
            render_frames(browser, frames_dir, count)
            if browser.errors:
                print("page errors:\n  " + "\n  ".join(browser.errors[:10]), file=sys.stderr)
            encode(frames_dir, args.out, args.fps)
        finally:
            shutil.rmtree(frames_dir, ignore_errors=True)
    print(f"{args.out} ({args.out.stat().st_size / 1e6:.1f} MB)")
    return args.out


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# Pipeline self-test. Proves runner, seeding and logging work. Not a project experiment.
[experiment]
name = "smoke"
entrypoint = "digital_life.smoke:run"
hypothesis = "Same seed gives identical metrics; different seeds differ."

[params]
population = 20
steps = 50
def run(config_path: Path, seeds: list[int] | None = None, tag: str = "", overrides: list[str] | None = None, results_root: Path | None = None) -> Path:
    cfg = tomllib.loads(config_path.read_text())
    exp = cfg["experiment"]
    params = dict(cfg.get("params", {}))
    overrides = list(overrides or [])
    for o in overrides:
        k, v = parse_override(o)
        params[k] = v
    seeds = list(seeds or exp.get("seeds", [0]))
    fn = load_entrypoint(exp["entrypoint"])

    stamp = datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ")
    out = (results_root or REPO / "experiments" / "results") / exp["name"] / (stamp + (f"_{tag}" if tag else ""))
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    shutil.copy(config_path, out / "config.toml")

    prov = provenance()
    finals = {}
    for seed in seeds:
        sdir = out / f"seed-{seed}"
        log = RunLog(sdir)
        seed_everything(seed)
        t0, started = time.perf_counter(), utc_now()
        error = None
        try:
            finals[seed] = fn(params, seed, log) or {}
        except Exception as ex:  # record the failure; a crash is a result too
            error = f"{type(ex).__name__}: {ex}"
            finals[seed] = None
        finally:
            log.close()
        record = {
            "experiment": exp["name"],
            "hypothesis": exp.get("hypothesis"),
            "entrypoint": exp["entrypoint"],
            "params": params,
            "overrides": list(overrides),
            "seed": seed,
            "started": started,
            "seconds": round(time.perf_counter() - t0, 3),
            "final_metrics": finals[seed],
            "error": error,
            "provenance": prov,
        }
        (sdir / "record.json").write_text(json.dumps(record, indent=2) + "\n")
        print(f"seed {seed}: {'ERROR ' + error if error else finals[seed]}")

    summary = {"experiment": exp["name"], "config": str(config_path), "seeds": seeds, "per_seed": finals, "across_seeds": summarise(finals), "provenance": prov}
    (out / "summary.json").write_text(json.dumps(summary, indent=2) + "\n")
    if prov["git_dirty"]:
        print("note: working tree had uncommitted changes; commit before runs you plan to cite")
    print(f"results: {out.relative_to(REPO) if out.is_relative_to(REPO) else out}")
    return out

# Viewer

**Commands:** `python viewer/bundle.py RUN_DIR -o run.html` writes one self-contained page you open from file://; `python viewer/capture.py run.html out.mp4 --from 0 --to 400 --step 0.5 --fps 30 [--bee ID]` renders it to video headless.

The viewer replays any run directory written by `experiments/run.py` (log format 1, described in `docs/BUILD_NOTES.md`). It reads only the logs, so what you see is what the run recorded.

## What the page shows

- The maze, the hive with its entrances, and the bloom. The patch in season is drawn in flower; the other sites are faint dashed outlines.
- A light colour wash for the season, with the season and year in the top right.
- Bees in warm yellow. The thin ring around each bee is its life left, out of the life cap (3 x base life). The ring turns red below a quarter of base life. A green dot means the bee is carrying from bloom. A stunned bee has a red edge.
- Hornets as orange-brown diamonds with a dark band. A dashed line joins a chasing hornet to its target.
- Sound ripples spreading to the hearing radius (10 cells): sound 1 in teal, sound 2 in magenta.
- A red flash on each sting, a gold sparkle on each hatching, a gold pulse on each delivery, and a grey fade where a bee died.
- The side panel. With nothing selected it shows the colony now and this season's deliveries, stings, hatchings and deaths, plus a key. Select a bee to see its life, what it is doing, its recent decisions (trigger, intent, sound, remember, say), what it has written to memory, and what it heard at home. Select a hornet to see its genes.

Positions are interpolated between ticks, so playback is smooth at any speed.

## Controls

- Play or pause with the button or the space bar. Left and right arrows step one tick.
- Drag the timeline to scrub. The speed menu sets ticks per second.
- Click or tap a bee or hornet to select it. Selection hit-tests the position it is drawn at. Click empty ground or press Escape to clear.
- Wheel or pinch to zoom around the pointer, drag to pan, double-click to fit the map again.
- Link to a moment with `#t=TICK&bee=ID` after the file name.

## Capture mode and video

`capture.py` loads the page with `#capture&from=T0&to=T1&step=S[&bee=ID][&view=x0,y0,x1,y1]`. In this mode the controls are hidden, nothing animates on its own, and the page exposes `window.__capture.count` and `window.__capture.frame(i)`, which draws tick `T0 + i * S`. Every effect is a function of the gap between the frame's tick and the event's tick, so a frame looks the same whatever order frames are drawn in. The test suite checks that the same frame gives byte-identical screenshots.

```bash
# a still of one moment, following bee 3
python viewer/capture.py run.html still.png --from 98 --bee 3
# video of ticks 0 to 400, 2 frames per tick at 30 fps (about 27 seconds), zoomed on part of the map
python viewer/capture.py run.html out.mp4 --from 0 --to 400 --step 0.5 --fps 30 --view 0,10,40,40
```

Capture drives Playwright's `chrome-headless-shell` through the DevTools protocol over a pipe (`--remote-debugging-pipe`), so it needs no Python packages beyond the standard library. It looks for the shell in `$VIEWER_CHROME`, then in `[REDACTED:path-outside-repo]`. Frames are written to a scratch directory on `/dev/shm` and deleted once ffmpeg (libx264, yuv420p) has encoded them. On the shared 4-core build VM, under load from other jobs, capture ran at 5 to 8 frames per second.

## Files

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `bundle.py` | Inlines `src/` and the run's logs into one HTML page. State and events are gzip-compressed and base64-encoded; the browser decompresses them with `DecompressionStream`. |
| `capture.py`, `cdp.py` | Headless capture to PNG or MP4, and a minimal DevTools client. |
| `src/data.js` | Decodes the run and builds the indices: ticks, sounds, effects, and each bee's history. |
| `src/draw_map.js`, `src/draw_live.js` | The fixed world, and the moving things and effects at a fractional tick. |
| `src/panel.js`, `src/input.js`, `src/app.js` | The side panel, pointer input, and playback, controls and capture mode. |
| `fixtures/make_fixture.py` | Writes `fixtures/synthetic-run/`, a small scripted run in the log format used for development and tests. It is a test fixture, not a result. |
| `test_viewer.py` | Smoke tests: bundling, loading from file://, rendering a frame, click selection, and deterministic capture. |

## Tests

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest viewer/test_viewer.py -q
VIEWER_RUNS_ROOT=experiments/results .venv/bin/python -m pytest viewer/test_viewer.py -q   # also loads real runs
```

The browser tests are skipped when the headless shell is not installed. By default they also load up to three real runs found under `experiments/results/`.

## Limits

- One run per page. Comparing conditions side by side means opening two pages.
- The page needs a browser with `DecompressionStream` (Chrome 80+, Firefox 113+, Safari 16.4+).
- A full 2,000-tick run bundles to about 130 KB for scripted bees. AI runs carry more decision text, so their pages will be larger.

The viewer is built, tested and pushed to `origin/viewer` as 12 small commits. I haven't merged it or touched main. All 8 smoke tests pass. They ran against the synthetic fixture and against two real 2,000-tick runs from the main build's scripted-bee and random-bee sims. Those two runs went to /dev/shm with no model calls and have been deleted; they were a viewer check, not results to cite.

**Commands** (also the first line of `viewer/README.md`):
```bash
../digital-life/.venv/bin/python viewer/bundle.py RUN_DIR -o run.html
../digital-life/.venv/bin/python viewer/capture.py run.html out.mp4 --from 0 --to 400 --step 0.5 --fps 30 [--bee ID] [--view x0,y0,x1,y1]
../digital-life/.venv/bin/python viewer/capture.py run.html still.png --from 98 --bee 3
VIEWER_RUNS_ROOT=experiments/results ../digital-life/.venv/bin/python -m pytest viewer/test_viewer.py -q
```

**What works (items 1 to 7):**
- **Bundle:** one HTML file with the run's logs compressed inside. It opens from file:// with no server. A full real run bundles to 130 to 158 KB.
- **Page:** it has everything on your list. Bees that share a cell are spread slightly apart so each one can be seen and clicked; before that, 4 live bees showed as 2. Bees and hornets also have a minimum size on screen, so the full 80 x 48 map is readable at 1280 x 720.
- **Capture mode:** each frame is drawn from the logs alone. The tests check that the same frame always gives an identical screenshot, and that click, play, scrub, zoom, pan and pinch work.
- **Capture script:** it drives the headless shell directly over a pipe, so it needs no extra Python packages. Frames go to /dev/shm and are deleted after ffmpeg encodes them. The last check produced a 1280x720 H.264 file with 121 frames.
- **Extra:** clicking a hornet shows its genes. You didn't ask for this.

**For the orchestrator:**
- **Tests not in `make test`:** `pyproject.toml` has `testpaths = ["tests"]`, so `make test` skips `viewer/test_viewer.py`. Adding `viewer` to that list is a change outside `viewer/`, so I left it.
- **Traces:** the hooks wrote nothing to `agent_traces/` while this headless session ran. The export should happen when the session ends, so commit `agent_traces/` with the merge.
- **Capture speed:** 5 to 8 frames per second on the shared VM, which had a load near 7 on 4 cores. At that rate a 2-minute video at 30 fps takes about 8 to 12 minutes.
- **Life ring:** the ring shows life out of the cap (3 x base life), so a newborn bee shows a third of a ring. That's accurate, but a viewer might misread it as low life.
